q: How does a Kalinganagar ferrochrome plant count chrome ore in Scope 3?
title: Ferrochrome: chrome ore in Scope 3
short: Chrome ore bought from Sukinda valley mines is a purchased good, Scope 3 category 1: tonnes times a factor for mining and processing, ideally from the mine. Trucking it to the plant is category 4 if you pay for the freight.
audience: Ferrochrome plants in Kalinganagar and Jajpur buying chrome ore from Odisha's Sukinda valley

ul: Category 1: ore tonnes times the mine's figure per tonne. Ask the mine for its diesel, explosives and electricity per tonne if it has no published number.
Category 4: tonne kilometres by truck or rail times a factor for the mode, when you pay the transporter.

p: Ore drying or briquetting inside your own plant is Scope 1. Electricity your plant buys is Scope 2.
It is small next to the furnace, but EU buyers asking for a cradle to gate figure expect it. A mine figure based on its own diesel is better than a generic number.

senseible: Senseible reads the energy invoices behind the making stage into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, and keeps material invoices on the Scope 3 trail. Material factors come from your supplier or a named database and are labelled with their source, so the product figure can be traced line by line.
